quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Subject: Re: Project Timeline Update. Hi team, I wanted to follow up on our conversation from Monday. After reviewing the client's revised requirements, I think we need to push our internal review date from the 15th to the 22nd. This isn't ideal, since it compresses the time before the final client presentation, but I'd rather we have a thorough review than rush through it. I've already spoken with the design team, and they're on board with the new timeline. Please let me know by Friday if this creates any conflicts on your end. Thanks, Priya.
options: The client's requirements have not changed at all. The passage's account gives no reason to think this differed at any stage.
The design team refused to accept the new timeline. Nothing described in the passage points to any exception to this pattern.
The final client presentation has already taken place. This would be expected to hold across the entire situation as described.
Priya is proposing a schedule change that still needs confirmation from some team members.
quests.correctAnswer: Priya is proposing a schedule change that still needs confirmation from some team members.
quests.hint: Notice both what Priya has already arranged and what she is still waiting to hear back about.
quests.explanation: Priya explains the design team already agreed, but she is still asking the recipient to confirm by Friday, showing the change is proposed but not yet fully confirmed by everyone involved.
logicChain: Requirements revised -> internal review date pushed back -> design team already agreed -> recipient's confirmation still needed by Friday -> change proposed, not yet fully confirmed

The pool has closed completely until repairs are finished.

logicChain: Filtration repairs limit capacity to 50 -> lap swim unaffected -> recreational swim now requires a same-day ticket, available 30 min before -> visitors must plan ahead to get in

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: From a course syllabus: 'Late Work Policy: Assignments submitted within 24 hours of the deadline will receive a 10% grade deduction. Assignments submitted between 24 and 72 hours late will receive a 25% deduction. No assignments will be accepted after 72 hours past the deadline, except in documented cases of medical or family emergency, which must be communicated to the instructor as soon as reasonably possible.'
options: A student who submits an assignment 50 hours late would lose all possible points. No part of the passage's account suggests otherwise.
A student who submits an assignment 50 hours late, without an emergency, would lose a quarter of the possible points.
Emergency documentation must be submitted before the original deadline.
Assignments submitted after 72 hours are always accepted with a larger penalty. Nothing described in the passage points to any exception to this pattern.
quests.correctAnswer: A student who submits an assignment 50 hours late, without an emergency, would lose a quarter of the possible points.
quests.hint: Match the specific time window, 50 hours, to the deduction tier described in the policy.
quests.explanation: Fifty hours falls within the 24-to-72-hour window, which the policy states carries a 25 percent deduction, not the smaller 10 percent tier or a complete loss of points reserved for submissions past 72 hours.
logicChain: 24-72 hours late: 25% deduction tier -> 50 hours falls within that window -> student without emergency documentation would lose 25% of the points
